steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Individualist cultures (e.g. USA, UK) prioritise personal goals, independence and individual rights. Collectivist cultures (e.g. Japan, China) prioritise group harmony, interdependence and social obligations. These values affect communication styles, conformity and self-concept.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: High-context cultures (e.g. Japan, Arab nations) rely heavily on NVC, context and shared understanding - much is left unsaid. Low-context cultures (e.g. Germany, USA) rely on explicit, direct verbal communication - meaning is in the words.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Cultural differences in conformity: collectivist cultures show higher conformity rates (Smith & Bond's meta-analysis). This reflects different values - conformity is seen positively as maintaining group harmony in collectivist cultures, but negatively as weakness in individualist cultures.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Culture and self-concept: independent self-construal (individualist - self is separate from others) vs interdependent self-construal (collectivist - self is defined through relationships). Markus & Kitayama showed these different self-views affect cognition, emotion and motivation.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Individualist = ME first (independence, direct). Collectivist = US first (interdependence, indirect). High-context = read between the lines. Low-context = say what you mean. WEIRD = Western, Educated, Industrialised, Rich, Democratic. Most psych participants are WEIRD - this is a bias problem.
